preregistration.expected_outcome:
Outperforms, with stability the remaining risk. On the development seeds flag F1 on
all_categorical improved by +0.17 (95% CI +0.13 to +0.21, Holm p 0.0002) with no budget or
stability regression; in a development comparison bagging raised flag stability from 0.73
(v1) to 0.76 against the default's 0.74. Round 2 showed the stability gap varies by seed
(v1 was 0.70 vs 0.76 there), so a confirmation-seed stability shortfall beyond 0.05 would
make it fail.
preregistration.hypothesis:
discrete-budget-v1 improved flag F1 on all-categorical data but failed on stability (round 2:
flag Jaccard 0.70 vs the default's 0.76): its ranking shifts between fits, so rows near the
budget cut change. Bagging the ranking -- averaging the default's combined score over 5 fits
on 80% subsamples before flagging the review budget's top rows -- steadies it. Hypothesis:
on all_categorical, flag F1 improves over the default with no false-positive-budget,
ranking or stability regression; every other scenario runs the default unchanged.
(A tie-consistent cut was considered first and rejected on the development seeds: tied
groups never straddled the cut, and it changed nothing.)
